description:
## Problem
`validate_scale_factor` in `benchbox/core/benchmark_registry.py` rejects every scale factor that is not listed in a benchmark's `scale_options` (introduced by #332 to fix JoinOrder at SF 1). The lists are menus that became hard limits. They blocked SSB, TPC-DI and primitives runs at SF 100 on Snowflake (2026-10-13), and the data generators accept far more than the lists. TPC-DS already runs any in-range value and labels it; TPC-H refuses SF 2 before its own classifier (`benchbox/core/tpc_patterns.py`, `UNOFFICIAL_NONSTANDARD`) is reached.

## Decision (owner, 2026-11-11)
Relaxed for every benchmark except the two with fixed data. Listed values stay the recommended set.

## Change
1. `benchbox/core/catalog_schema.py`: add optional `scale_policy` to `BenchmarkMeta`, accepting only `fixed`.
2. `benchbox/core/benchmark_registry.yaml`: set `scale_policy: fixed` on `joinorder` and `metadata_primitives`. Change no `scale_options` value in this item.
3. `benchbox/core/benchmark_registry.py`, `validate_scale_factor`:
   - `tpcds` and `tpcds_obt` keep delegating to `validate_tpcds_scale`.
   - `scale_policy: fixed`: the value must be a listed one, as today (`ScaleFactorNotSupportedError`).
   - Every other benchmark: the value must be finite, at least `min_scale` (or the smallest listed value when `min_scale` is absent), at most 100000, and a whole number when it is 1 or more. Outside that, raise a `ValueError` subclass whose message states the range and the listed values.
   - Remove the ClickBench special case; ClickBench follows the general rule.
   - Give callers a way to learn whether an accepted value is a standard one (a return value or a small public helper). Standard means listed in `scale_options`; for `tpcds` it also includes the registry's `tpc_official_scale_options`, so an official SF 300 run is not called non-standard. The existing callers that ignore the result keep working.
4. `changelog.d/`: one fragment for the whole feature, covering the range rule, the non-standard note and the 0.01 minimum.
5. Tests: rewrite `tests/unit/core/test_scale_factor_validation.py` and the scale assertion in `tests/unit/core/ssb/test_ssb_family_plugin.py`, which pin the old rejections. Delete tests of the old allow-list; do not re-pin them.

## Not in this item
The 0.01 floor (`scale-factor-floor-0-01-20261111`); the note printed to users and MCP output (`scale-factor-nonstandard-note-surfaces-20261111`); site docs (`site-scale-factor-docs-20261111`); generator runs at large scales (`generator-validation-large-scales-20261111`).

## Decision gates
- Before editing, confirm on current `origin/develop` that `validate_scale_factor` still has the allow-list branch and the ClickBench branch, and list every caller with `rg 'validate_scale_factor\('`.
- If `tests/uat/matrix.py` or `scripts/export_docs_data.py` would change behaviour because of this item, stop and report: they must keep reading `scale_options` unchanged.
- If any caller depends on `ScaleFactorNotSupportedError` for a non-fixed benchmark other than the two tests named above, stop and report it.

## Guardrails
- Work only in the feature worktree, never the primary clone. Run `make agent-write-preflight` first.
- Touch only the files this item names. Report anything adjacent as noticed, not changed.
- No explanatory comments or docstrings in first-party code (`make comment-policy-check`).
- No edit to `CHANGELOG.md`; the feature carries one `changelog.d/` fragment.
- No full test tier, benchmark or data generation outside `make heavy-run` or a lock-taking target.
- Subagents make no tracker write, push nothing and open no pull request.
- `scale_options` keeps its meaning for the interactive picker, MCP `options`, the UAT matrix filter and the docs-data export.
- No new command-line flag and no change to any generator class.
